market_specific_notes: Los Angeles neuro-evaluation shoppers usually need a cleaner comparison of testing depth, report usefulness, and adult-versus-child fit instead of generic diagnosis language.
The best local comparison in Los Angeles is whether a clinic explains scope, turnaround, and what the written report is actually for.
local_vetting_points: Ask whether the evaluation is screening-only or a full diagnostic workup.
Ask whether the report is built for school, workplace, accommodations, treatment planning, or just confirmation.
Ask which age groups the clinician routinely evaluates.
typical_cost_ranges: Pricing in Los Angeles often shifts based on testing depth, interview time, collateral review, and report complexity.
A low quote is not meaningful if it excludes report quality or follow-up explanation.
payment_options: Ask whether the clinic is private pay only, offers superbills, or helps with reimbursement paperwork.
Ask whether intake, testing, scoring, feedback, and report delivery are billed together or separately.
wait_time_notes: Wait time should be judged by intake delay, testing date, and final report delivery together.
A fast intake call does not guarantee fast testing or fast reporting.
availability_notes: Availability should include adult-versus-child fit, tele-intake options, and realistic report turnaround after testing.
Los Angeles shoppers should explicitly compare telehealth intake convenience against in-person testing requirements before assuming the process is faster.
Ask whether cancellations meaningfully change timing or only move the first call earlier.
named_resources_or_providers: Los Angeles academic medical centers, psychology groups, and accommodations-oriented provider directories are usually more useful than generic testing-near-me lists.
Use modality fit, report purpose, and reimbursement handling as part of the comparison instead of brand familiarity alone.
city_intro_override: Los Angeles neuro-evaluation shoppers usually do better when they compare telehealth versus in-person workflow, report usefulness, and reimbursement reality before they compare branding.

primary_city_decision_block.title: How to choose an autism or ADHD evaluation provider in Los Angeles
items: Ask whether the clinic explains when telehealth intake works and when in-person testing is still required.
Ask whether the report is built for school, workplace, treatment planning, or only diagnostic confirmation.
Ask how long the real path is from intake to testing to final report delivery.
Ask whether the office handles private pay only, gives superbills, or supports reimbursement paperwork.
Ask whether the evaluator routinely works with adults, children, or both.

testing_scope_notes: Ask whether the clinic offers screening, diagnostic clarification, ADHD-focused testing, autism-focused testing, or a broader differential workup.
Testing depth should match the real decision you need to make.
insurance_reimbursement_notes: Ask whether the clinic accepts insurance, provides superbills, or expects full private-pay reimbursement follow-through from the patient.
Do not assume testing is covered just because intake is covered.
adult_vs_child_fit: Confirm whether the clinician routinely evaluates adults, children, or both, and whether the testing approach changes by age group.
report_turnaround_notes: Ask when the written report is delivered, whether feedback is separate, and whether accommodations-ready language is included when relevant.
